validated_work_order.understanding:
A custom report appends three synthetic rows — Uncategorized (uncategorized_id 'other'), Transfers ('transfer') and Off budget ('off_budget') — in categoryLists() at packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/ReportOptions.ts:348, :354 and :360, and parks them under the synthetic 'Uncategorized & Off budget' group (ReportOptions.ts:375-381) that categoryLists appends to categoryGroup at :406. All three are declared id: '', and that group is the only one whose members are not keyed by a uuid.

The duplicate-key warning comes from exactly one render site. With Mode=Total, Viz=Data Table and the default Group by=Category, ReportTableList takes the grouped branch (ReportTableList.tsx:28-30, data.groupedData) and renders each group's members at ReportTableList.tsx:73-87 with key={category.id}. The uncategorized group therefore emits three sibling keys of '' on every render and React logs 'Encountered two children with the same key'. 'Show empty rows' is what makes it unconditional: without it filterEmptyRows (filterEmptyRows.ts:16-24) drops synthetic rows whose amount is zero, so the keys only collide when at least two of the three survive. With it on, filterEmptyRows returns true for every member (grouped-spreadsheet.ts:158-162), so all three always render and all three keys always collide.

Two neighbouring key={item.id} / key={category.id} uses look like candidates and are not. ReportTableRow.tsx:97 puts the key on the single element that component returns, which is never an array child (RenderTableRow.tsx:34-44 renders it singly), so React ignores it. ReportTableList.tsx:55 and ReportTableHeader.tsx:87 key by index. CategorySelector.tsx:226 keys by id, but ReportSidebar.tsx:701-704 feeds it categories.grouped.filter(...) straight off useCategories() — never categoryLists()' output — so the synthetic group never reaches it.

This is a one-line fix and it changes nothing a person can see. I could not execute anything to confirm the warning: this checkout has no node_modules in either the root or packages/desktop-client, so no test or build runs. The claim rests on reading a closed set — three declared id: '' values and the one key={category.id} that consumes exactly those three members.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Three distinct report rows share one entity id (id: ''), and ReportTableList keys its sibling rows by that id, so three siblings collide on every render of the Category-grouped Data Table with 'Show empty rows' on.
validated_work_order.approach:
Change the key at the render site; do not touch the three entity identities. This is what the ticket asks for, and reading the code says it is also the only safe place to change it — id: '' is load-bearing downstream in ways a distinct id would silently break.

The check I ran for each candidate lookup that matches on id:

- filterHiddenItems.ts discriminates the three rows on item.uncategorized_id, not id — unaffected either way.
- recalculate.ts and custom-spreadsheet.ts:212-235 match a row with asset[groupByLabel] === (item.id ?? null) || (item.uncategorized_id && groupsByCategory). With id '' the first clause is false and the second carries the row; a distinct id would make the first clause false too, so amounts would not move.
- narrowCategoriesByConditions (budgetDataQuery.ts:126-166) builds its keep-set from the real category list and runs before categoryLists() appends the synthetic rows, so the synthetic block is never narrowed away. An existing test already pins this (custom-spreadsheet.test.ts:656).
- calculateLegend.ts:70-73 sets dataKey: item.id || item.name and custom-spreadsheet.ts:277 sets stacked[item.id || item.name] from the same expression, so giving the rows real ids would move both together — a wide, chart-visible change for no benefit here.
- showActivity.ts:57-79 is the one that decides it. For the Uncategorized row the drilldown passes field: 'category', id: '', uncategorizedId: 'other'; id && { ... } is falsy on the empty string, so no category condition is emitted. Give the row id: 'uncategorized' and the same click emits category is 'uncategorized', a filter that matches no category and turns the row's drilldown into an empty result — a behaviour change in the opposite direction from the ticket's goal.
- CategorySelector never sees these rows, so changing ids would not have broken its checkbox matching either — but it would have put a lie in the code for the next reader.

So: one line. At ReportTableList.tsx:77 replace key={category.id} with a key derived from the field that actually distinguishes these rows. recalculate (recalculate.ts:127) already copies uncategorized_id onto every row as uncategorizedId, and the type carries it (GroupedEntity, packages/loot-core/src/types/models/reports.ts:117), so the render site has what it needs without touching ReportOptions.ts:

    key={category.uncategorizedId ?? category.id}

For the three synthetic rows this yields 'other', 'transfer', 'off_budget'; for every real category uncategorizedId is undefined and the key stays the uuid it is today, so no existing row's key changes. Real category ids are uuids, so none can equal 'other'/'transfer'/'off_budget', and the three members live in a group with no real members, so the keys are distinct within the sibling list. Add a comment at that line saying why.

What this deliberately does not touch: the row values, the amounts, the group, the sidebar, the legend, and the graph dataKeys.

Reconciliation note: changing the key changes which DOM node React reuses for these three rows. ReportTableRow holds no per-row state, so there is nothing to leak between rows, and the change is in the direction of React doing the right thing — under duplicate keys it was already reusing the wrong nodes.

One surface, both faces planned here: the one-line code change plus a vitest file that renders ReportTableList directly with a fixture carrying the three synthetic rows and asserts no duplicate-key console.error, three distinct keys, and all three names present.

**How the previous plan's two objections are answered.**

(1) The v1 plan added an e2e case and an AC-6 with verify: "test" citing a Playwright file. That was wrong and I confirmed why: .sdlc/config.yml:172 sets verify.e2e: "", .github/workflows/ci-verify.yml:245-252 reads it, prints 'verify.e2e not configured - skipping' and exits 0 — so no CI job runs the Playwright suite, and .sdlc/config.yml is a forbidden path a work order cannot change. The v1 residual_risks entry claiming CI coverage of AC-1 rested on Playwright is therefore deleted rather than softened. This revision drops AC-6 and drops the packages/desktop-client/e2e/reports.test.ts entry from tests[] entirely; no file in the plan is now read only by a runner nobody invokes. The guard is covered twice by things that do run: the vitest file lands under packages/desktop-client/src/, which yarn test (lage test → desktop-client vitest --run, include glob src/**/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x) at vite.config.mts:406) does execute, and AC-1 stays verify: "browser" — QA boots the Vite dev server (env.boot: "yarn start"), which serves React's development build, so the warning is a real console.error, and .sdlc/agents/qa.md:152 fails any case that 'passed while throwing console errors'. Every QA case that touches this screen therefore proves AC-1 without a new file.

(2) The v1 AC-2, AC-4 and qa_script step 7 asked QA to compare against the pre-change rendering. That is not available: .sdlc/config.yml:103 gives QA one base_url booted from the PR and .sdlc/agents/qa.md:120 forbids anything else, and the demo budget's amounts are not stable between runs — createDemoBudget() (packages/loot-core/src/server/budgetfiles/app.ts:246) builds createBudget({ testMode: true }) from #mocks/budget, and packages/loot-core/src/mocks/random.ts:15 exports random = Platform.isPlaywright ? pseudoRandom : Math.random, deterministic only when the UA says Playwright (which packages/desktop-client/playwright.config.ts:20 forces and QA's own config does not). The repo already says so at packages/desktop-client/e2e/page-models/custom-report-page.ts:90. All three are restated below as invariants checkable inside one run against the PR's own build, with no baseline and no pinned amounts.

One correction to the reviewer's own suggested wording for AC-2, because taking it literally would write a criterion the code cannot satisfy: it says the three rows appear 'in order'. They do not. uncategorizedGroup.categories is declared [uncategorizedCategory, transferCategory, offBudgetCategory] (ReportOptions.ts:376), but grouped-spreadsheet.ts:193-200 re-sorts each group's members with sortData({ balanceTypeOp, sortByOp }), and sortData.ts:17-49 sorts by amount (default sortBy: 'desc' on totalDebts reverses to ascending). So the on-screen order is amount order, which varies with the generated budget. AC-2 below asserts the three names are each present exactly once under the group header, with a non-blank amount cell each, and says nothing about order. The fix does not change the sort either way.

It proves the three keys no longer collide at the one render site; it does not prove React's reconciliation of the real Data Table (with its header, totals row and interval columns) is warning-free.
